One or two sentences on what I learned.

<!-- ── Single labeled block ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
     One block inside `.compare` = a lone labeled box (still content-sized).
     A bare fenced block outside `.compare` needs no wrapper at all. -->

::: {.compare}
```python
result = [x**2 for x in range(10)]
print(result)
```
:::

<!-- ── Side by side ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
     Wrap plain fenced code blocks in `.compare`. Each block becomes a
     content-sized column—a box that hugs its code, with a centered
     language label above. Columns stack full-width on phones. -->

::: {.compare}
```python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
df.head()
```

```sql
SELECT *
FROM 'data.csv'
LIMIT 5;
```
:::

::: {.note}
Optional caveat or aside, placed right after a comparison, it tucks under it.
:::

<!-- ── Three columns ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
     Add `.column-page-right` to grant extra room: the left edge stays
     aligned with the text, columns extend rightward only as needed. -->

:::: {.compare .column-page-right}
```python
import pandas as pd
data = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
data.groupby("category")["value"].agg(["count", "mean"])
```

```r
library(data.table)
data = fread("data.csv")
data[, .(n = .N, mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE)), by = category]
```

````sql
-- SQL (use ```{.sql .duckdb} to label it DuckDB)
SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n, AVG(value) AS mean
FROM 'data.csv'
GROUP BY category;
````
::::
